from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Scaling dimensions changes our geometric intuition completely.",
            "A line segment grows to a circle, then sphere.",
            "The hypersphere equation defines points at distance R.",
            "Dimensions expand from one to three.",
            "Equation constraints points to a constant radius."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Warm-up: Scaling Dimensions", lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        line_seg = Line(LEFT, RIGHT).set_color(RED)
        circle = Circle(radius=0.7).set_color(GREEN)
        sphere = Sphere(radius=0.6).set_color(YELLOW).set_opacity(0.5)
        
        self.place_at_grid(line_seg, 'B2')
        self.play(Create(line_seg))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Transform(line_seg, circle))
        self.wait(0.5)
        self.play(Transform(line_seg, sphere))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        equation = MathTex("x_1^2 + x_2^2 + \\dots + x_n^2 = R^2").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(equation, 'E3')
        self.play(Write(equation))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(TEAL))
        # Visualizing dimensions (simple representations)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(ORANGE))
        self.play(Indicate(equation))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "In higher dimensions, hypersphere volume shrinks to zero.",
            "Think of a robot searching high-dimensional space.",
            "Its net captures almost nothing in higher dimensions.",
            "Cube vs sphere volume as n grows.",
            "Robot fails to capture volume effectively."
        ]

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        robot = SVGMobject("robot_scout_search.svg") if False else Square(color=GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(robot, 'D2')
        self.play(DrawBorderThenFill(robot))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        net = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW)
        self.place_at_grid(net, 'D4')
        self.play(Create(net))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(RED))
        cube = Square(color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(cube, 'B5')

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(PURPLE))
        self.play(robot.animate.set_color(PURPLE), net.animate.set_color(PURPLE))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Almost all hypersphere volume resides near the surface.",
            "Imagine an orange with a massive, heavy peel.",
            "The inner fruit becomes mathematically negligible.",
            "Peel represents concentrated surface volume.",
            "Interior density fades as dimensions increase."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Crusty Shell: Concentration of Mass", lecture_lines)
        
        # Color palette for highlighting
        highlight_color = YELLOW
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Almost all hypersphere volume resides near the surface.
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        circle_shell = Circle(radius=1.5, color=BLUE, stroke_width=10)
        self.place_at_grid(circle_shell, 'C2')
        self.play(Create(circle_shell))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Imagine an orange with a massive, heavy peel.
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        orange = Circle(radius=1.5, color=ORANGE, fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(orange, 'C2')
        self.play(FadeIn(orange))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # The inner fruit becomes mathematically negligible.
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        inner_fruit = Circle(radius=0.2, color=RED, fill_opacity=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(inner_fruit, 'C2')
        self.play(GrowFromCenter(inner_fruit))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Peel represents concentrated surface volume.
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(highlight_color))
        peel_label = Text("Peel: ~99% Volume", font_size=18, color=ORANGE)
        self.place_at_grid(peel_label, 'B4')
        self.play(Write(peel_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===

        self.place_at_grid(fade_label, 'D4')

        self.setup_layout("Real-world Application: Data Science", lecture_lines)

outline.topic: The Geometry of High-Dimensional Spheres: Beyond 3D

sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Scaling Dimensions
sections.content: Establish the foundation by visualizing the growth of a hyper-cube (L-norm) versus the containment of a sphere as dimensions increase. Define the hypersphere equation: x₁² + x₂² + ... + xₙ² = R².
sections.example: Visualizing a 1D line segment, 2D circle, and 3D sphere to establish the pattern of enclosure.

sections.title: The Paradox of Volume: Where did it go?
sections.content: Explain the counter-intuitive behavior where the volume of a unit hypersphere approaches zero as the dimension n approaches infinity, even though the radius is 1.
sections.example: A 'Robot Scout' trying to capture a volume of space; as it gains more dimensions, it finds its 'net' captures almost nothing of the surrounding hyper-cube.

sections.title: The Crusty Shell: Concentration of Mass
sections.content: Explain that in high dimensions, almost all the volume of a hypersphere is concentrated in a thin 'crust' near the surface. The interior becomes essentially empty.
sections.example: An 'Orange-Slice' analogy: imagine peeling an orange where the peel is the vast majority of the volume, and the fruit inside is mathematically negligible.

sections.title: Visualization Techniques: Projection and Slicing
sections.content: Introduce how we represent these objects via 2D projections (Shadows) and cross-sectional slices. Discuss how 'distance' behaves differently in high-dimensional space.
sections.example: Using a 3D light-box to project a 4D hypersphere onto a 2D screen, creating a pulsing, morphing geometric shadow.

sections.title: Real-world Application: Data Science
sections.content: Connect high-dimensional spheres to the 'Curse of Dimensionality' in Machine Learning, where data points become equidistant and spheres are used to define boundary classifications.
sections.example: An AI facial recognition system classifying 'faces' as points on a high-dimensional hypersphere surface to distinguish between different individuals.
